modernize/animation_sync.title: Phase-lagged square motion
modernize/animation_sync.description: Ten circles begin the same four-leg motion at evenly offset times; the scene uses ordinary awaited plays and leaves same-frame completion handoffs to the scheduler.
walkthrough: run creates ten red circles, labels them E0 through E9, and starts one rotate coroutine for each. Each coroutine waits for its phase offset before beginning; the largest offset is 1.125 seconds, so the repeated square movement reads as a wave rather than a simultaneous start.

rotate moves a circle through four 40-unit corners, with each leg lasting 1,000 ms, then repeats. Consecutive await this.play calls express the sequence directly. If a leg ends partway through a render frame, the completion-boundary scheduler automatically advances the following leg through the remaining time; this scene does not calculate or receive an overshoot value.
Camera2DController makes the large square path easier to inspect. It is independent of the animation scheduler and can be removed when the example is used only as a timing test.
experiments: Change the phase divisor from n * 0.8 to n * 2.0 and compare the tighter start wave without changing any animation duration.
Set the leg duration to a value that does not divide a typical frame interval, then compare the corner transitions at different display refresh rates.
